Re: LD 561 - An Act to Ensure Subsidy Reimbursements for Certain Child Care Providers

Senator Ingwersen, Representative Meyer and members of the Joint Standing Committee on Health and Human Services,

Thank you for the opportunity to share in information in support of LD 561, An Act to Ensure Subsidy Reimbursements for Certain Child Care Providers.

This bill would require the Department to reimburse child care providers under the Child Care Affordability Program (CCAP) based on generally accepted payment practices, which includes paying providers based on enrollment instead of the current practice which pays providers based on the attendance of each individual child.

Payments to providers based on enrollment, prospective payments, reduced co-pays, and child care slot contracts are new requirements under the Child Care Development Block Grant (CCDBG) and OCFS will be implementing payments based on enrollment this year. OCFS supports this bill since it aligns with the State's General Fund investment in CCAP. The forthcoming Baxter child care management system is being developed to pay providers based on enrollment and to meet other federal requirements. That system will go live later this year.

OCFS urges the Committee to vote ought to pass on LD 561.

Please feel free to contact me if you have any questions during your deliberation of this bill.

Sincerely,

Bobbi L. Johnson, LMSW Director Office of Child and Family Services Maine Department of Health and Human Services
10037143:
Testimony of Courtney Wood before the Committee on Health and Human Services
in support of LD 561: An Act to Ensure Subsidy Reimbursements for Certain Child Care Providers
March 14, 2025
Senator Ingwersen, Representative Meyer, and honorable members of the Committee on Health and Human Services, my name is Courtney Wood and I'm the Director of Child Care Services for the Down East Family YMCA in Hancock County. I support LD 561: An Act to Ensure Subsidy Reimbursements for Certain Child Care Providers.
Collectively, the 15 YMCAs in Maine are the largest childcare provider in the state. We serve thousands of children in our early childhood education programs, before/afterschool programs, and summer camp. These programs provide children with safe, nurturing and enriching care, and are a critical component of our state's infrastructure to support working parents and our economy.
The current attendance-based reimbursement payment practice for children on the Child Care Affordability Program (CCAP) is a financial and administrative burden for providers. This payment practice causes significant hardship for those providers that participate, and discourages others from accepting children on subsidy. Providers have no way of knowing, or control over, the children's attendance, and therefore cannot predict their payments. Further, the fixed costs of care - including staffing and keeping the building open - do not decrease if those children are absent, yet our payments from the State do decrease. Frankly, providers are left subsidizing the subsidy program, and this is simply not sustainable or fair.
At our Y, we care for more than 295 children at any given time. Last year, we served 241 children on subsidy. Considering that the CCAP reimbursement rate is lower than our private pay rate and that we only got paid for the actual time kids attended, we lost $178,454 last year alone. Further, we had to track 241 children's hours, and spend time billing separately for 241 children. We want to support our community and make a difference in the lives of children, but this program is burdening our organization with incredibly high administrative and financial costs.
The shift from attendance-based to enrollment-based reimbursement for CCAP is a critical step in making this important program work for families and providers. Enrollment-based reimbursement is a more stable and sustainable funding mechanism for providers, and better aligns with the payment practices of our private-pay families.
Respectfully submitted, Courtney Wood

Testimony of Diane Dickerson, CEO, Bangor Region YMCA before the Committee on Health and Human Services in support of
LD 561: An Act to Ensure Subsidy Reimbursements for Certain Child Care Providers March 14, 2025
Senator Ingwersen, Representative Meyer, and honorable members of the Committee on Health and Human Services, my name is Diane Dickerson and I am the proud CEO of the Bangor Region YMCA, where we serve the region that includes more than 25 towns and 10 School Districts. We have a robust Child Development Program and accept children on the Child Care Affordability Program (CCAP) as well as provide additional financial assistance we privately raise to ensure all our families are well-served and have the opportunity for early childhood education and before and afterschool enrichment programming. I strongly support LD 561: An Act to Ensure Subsidy Reimbursements for Certain Child Care Providers.
Collectively, the 15 YMCAs in Maine are the largest childcare provider in the state. We serve thousands of children in our early childhood education programs, before/afterschool programs, and summer camp. These programs provide children with safe, nurturing and enriching care, and are a critical component of our state's infrastructure to support working parents and our economy.
The current attendance-based reimbursement payment practice for children on CCAP is a financial and administrative burden for providers. This payment practice causes significant hardship for those providers that participate, and disincentivizes others from accepting children on subsidy. Providers have no way of knowing, or control over, the children's attendance, and therefore cannot predict their payments. Further, the fixed costs of care - including staffing and keeping the building open - do not decrease if those children are absent, yet our payments from the State do decrease. Frankly, providers are left subsidizing the subsidy program, and this is simply not sustainable or fair.
The shift from attendance-based to enrollment-based reimbursement for CCAP is a critical step in making this important program work for families and providers. Enrollment-based reimbursement is a more stable and sustainable funding mechanism for providers, and better aligns with the payment practices of our private-pay families. This bill can help ensure that the Bangor Region YMCA, the region's largest facilitybased childcare program, remains able to accept children on subsidy, knowing that we will receive consistent payments. This can increase access to affordable, high-quality childcare for low-income families in the greater Bangor area, which is greatly needed. Our region has the 3rd lowest percent of high-quality childcare sites and the rate of child poverty (15.5%) exceeds the State of Maine rate (12.3%).
With more stable funding for our Early Childhood Education and our Before and After School Programs, the Bangor Region YMCA can invest in better facilities, hire better trained staff, and continue offering quality care for the children of our region. This will lead to improved academic, social, and behavioral outcomes for children.
On behalf of our children, families, staff and the community we serve, I respectfully ask for your support of LD 561: An Act to Ensure Subsidy Reimbursements for Certain Child Care Providers.
Respectfully submitted,

Senator lngwersen, Representative Meyer, and distinguished members of the Health and Human Services Committee, my name is Heather Marden, Co-Executive Director of the Maine
Association for the Education of Young Children (MaineAEYC) and former early childhood educator of 20 years.
MaineAEYC promotes high-qua/ity early learning for each and every child, birth through age 8,
by connecting practice, policy, and research. We advance a diverse, dynamic early childhood
profession and support all who care for, educate, and work on behalf of young children.

The U.S. Treasury Department has determined that the existing child-care system in the country is considered "unworkable" due to notable market failures that restrict access to quality care for many families. Studies reveal that most for-profit providers in this $60 billion industry work with margins of less than 1%.

Maine currently has around 1400 licensed child care programs of which the majority are part of our small business infrastructure in the state. Communities and families around the state know all too well the devastating effects of when one of these small businesses succumbs to financial hardships. LD 561 will provide consistent, stable funding for child care businesses through the Child Care Affordability Program which helps lower-income families in Maine afford and access child care. This legislation will ensure in state statute that the change from current reimbursement practices that only reimbursing for certain "allowable" absences of children to instead reimbursing for the full enrolled hours of the child.
As you are aware, the federal government is currently in a period of significant volatility when it comes to child care program rules and funding. While there is an ongoing effort at the federal

level to improve payment practices, the uncertainty surrounding the future of these policies

open and provide quality care.

child care businesses. However, the unpredictability of federal policies means we cannot solely
rely on federal rules to ensure these changes will remain in place.

This is why I am asking for your support in making these changes permanent by adding clear and explicit language to existing state statute. By incorporating this language into law, we can
solidify the reimbursement practices needed at the state level, ensuring that child care businesses in Maine have the certainty and financial stability they need to continue providing
high-quality services to families.

The state is already budgeting for this change, and this request would simply be a technical language addition to existing law. lt's a practical step that provides long-term security for our
child care providers. By securing these changes at the state level, we ensure that even in the
face of federal uncertainty, Maine's child care businesses will continue to receive the support they need.

Good morning Senator lngwersen, Representative Meyer, and esteemed members of the Joint Standing
Committee on Health and Human Services. My name is Joe Baldacci, and l am privileged to represent Senate District 9, which includes Bangor and Hermon. I am here to testify in support of my bill LD 561, "An Act to Ensure
Subsidy Reimbursements for Certain Child Care Providers."
I will keep this testimony brief. As we know, Maine is still suffering from a child care shortage. ln order to take steps to address this, we need to make sure that our child care facilities remain open and have what they need to
operate.
During the pandemic, many different states implemented new policies about how child care subsidy reimbursement payments were paid to providers. They shifted from basing the subsidy reimbursements on attendance to basing them on how many children were enrolled in a program. Typically, enrollment numbers are
higher than attendance, because children can be absent for a variety of reasons, such as illness or vacation. The switch from attendance to enrollment based subsidy payments helped stabilize the child care sector from a pandemic induced collapse.
From a study done by Child Care Aware of America, 82% of the total number of providers that accepted subsidies in January and February of 2020 also accepted them in July and August, indicating they were able to remain open
By employing this practice here in Maine, l think we can make a positive impact in stabilizing the child care sector
and keeping or child care centers open and operating with qualified individuals.
Thank you very much for your time and consideration.
Joe Baldacci
